<!-- file: docs/agent-native/install-order.md -->
# Agent-native phase 1.3: install order for a new studio

Status: read from `package.json` files, `tooling/`, `packages/ignition/scripts/`, `docs/native/NITRO_V1_HOST_INTEGRATION.md`, `.github/workflows/` and `apps/example`. No command here was run on this machine (4.9 GB free, no install allowed). Where a command comes from CI or a script, the source is named. UNVERIFIED marks a step the files do not settle.

Nothing here is published to npm. `compatibility.v1.json` records `distribution: github-release-tarballs`, `npm: not-used`, and no tag or release exists for the Forge packages. Every `@nitro-forge/*` package is `0.0.0` at the root or `0.1.0` per package and resolves through `workspace:*`. A consumer outside this monorepo has no installable `@nitro-forge/ignition`, engine or `studio-layout` today.

## The chain

Each step needs the one above it. Step 7 fails at first render if step 6 is skipped, and every studio-workspace component throws without `StudioUIProvider` ("No substitute UI is installed").

| # | Step | Command or edit | Registry add can do it? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Toolchain | Node >=24.3.0, pnpm 12.18.0 (`packageManager`), Rust with `cargo`, Xcode for Apple, Android NDK and `cargo-ndk` for Android | No |
| 1 | `@nitro-forge/ignition` (native host) | see below | No (decision 4) |
| 2 | Engine package, for example `@nitro-forge/tally` | `workspace:*` dependency, Rust crate linked through `nf-sys` | No (decision 3) |
| 3 | `@nitro-forge/studio-layout` | `workspace:*` dependency, private package | No (decision 3) |
| 4 | `@nitro-forge/icons` | registry item `forge-icon` | Yes, plus peers |
| 5 | NYC-Tron tarballs | URL dependencies from `tooling/nyc-tron.json` | No for the packages, yes for registry items that wrap them |
| 6 | Theme CSS | generated `theme.css` or `theme.native.css`, plus an import | Files yes, build step no |
| 7 | `StudioUIProvider` and host | registry items `studio-ui-provider`, `nyc-tron-host` plus app code | Files yes, host wiring is app code |
| 8 | Studio components | registry items from `03-design-handoff.md` | Yes |

Registry mechanics (decision 28, corrected by decision 45): the built `r/*.json` files are committed in each repo and served from `raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/<ref>/r/{name}.json`. `<ref>` is a moving branch (`master` for `@nitro-forge`, `main` for `@nyc-tron`) until the owner cuts release tags, then `node tooling/registry/set-ref.mjs <tag> [<tag>]` pins both. A consumer adds an item with `npx shadcn@latest add @nitro-forge/<item>`. The `@nyc-tron` items it depends on resolve only once NYC-Tron's `r/` is on its `main` branch. Pin the CLI version too (`npx shadcn@4.23.0`) if you need a reproducible install, because `@latest` moves. A live fetch from raw.githubusercontent.com has not been run. UNVERIFIED.

### Step 0. Toolchain

- Node >=24.3.0 and pnpm 12.18.0 come from the root `package.json` (`engines`, `packageManager`). CI runs `corepack enable && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` on Node 24 (`.github/workflows/ignition-v1-integration.yml`).
- Rust: `cargo` is required for every native archive. The Apple script builds three targets (`aarch64-apple-ios`, `aarch64-apple-ios-sim`, `x86_64-apple-ios`); install them with `rustup target add` (the script does not install them).
- Android: `ANDROID_NDK_HOME` must point at the NDK the Expo app uses, and `cargo-ndk` must be installed.
- The workspace pins one Nitro runtime for the whole graph: `react-native-nitro-modules` and `nitro-core` at `1.0.0-alpha.nightly.136.gdb81de61bd32` (`pnpm-workspace.yaml` overrides). Metro is pinned at 0.87.2 and ten dependencies carry pnpm patches (`patches/`). A consumer outside the monorepo needs the same pins. UNVERIFIED: whether a clean consumer app builds without the patches.

### Step 1. `@nitro-forge/ignition` (host, native module, Nitrogen output)

From the repo root:

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm --filter @nitro-forge/ignition codegen          # nitrogen; output is committed, regenerate only after a spec change
pnpm --filter @nitro-forge/ignition typecheck
pnpm --filter @nitro-forge/ignition exec vitest run tests/nitro-host.test.ts
cargo test --locked -p nf-sys && cargo build --locked -p nf-sys
```

Native archives, run before Expo prebuild or build (`docs/native/NITRO_V1_HOST_INTEGRATION.md`):

```bash
bash packages/ignition/scripts/build-apple.sh        # writes packages/ignition/native/ForgeRust.xcframework
ANDROID_NDK_HOME=/path/to/ndk bash packages/ignition/scripts/build-android.sh   # default ABIs: armeabi-v7a arm64-v8a x86 x86_64, platform 24
bash packages/ignition/scripts/build-android.sh arm64-v8a                       # a subset
```

Facts to know:

- `build-apple.sh` refuses to run if `native/ForgeRust.xcframework` already exists ("Remove the previous generated ... before rebuilding").
- The integration doc says the Apple archive covers arm64 iPhone and Apple Silicon simulators, not Intel simulators. The script builds `x86_64-apple-ios` and lipos it into the simulator slice. The script and the doc disagree. The script is the later source of truth; UNVERIFIED which is right on a real Intel simulator.
- iOS minimum is 16 (`Package.swift`, `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=16.0`). The Expo example sets Android `minSdkVersion` 29. The Android script builds with `--platform 24`.
- Nitro v1 links through SwiftPM on Apple (`experiments.swiftPackageManager: true` in `apps/example/app.json`); the podspec `NitroForgeV1.podspec` is for React Native dependency discovery only.
- For tests without a device, `cargo build --locked -p nf-cli` builds the JSON-lines host (`@nitro-forge/ignition/cli`).
- Not run on this machine: Rust tests, Android NDK link, Xcode link, any device launch. The integration doc itself lists those as not run at integration time. UNVERIFIED on current commit.

### Step 2. Engine package

Add the package as a `workspace:*` dependency, for example `"@nitro-forge/tally": "workspace:*"` (`apps/example/package.json` shows all of them). Each engine package depends on `@nitro-forge/ignition` and has no install command of its own. The Rust side is already linked: `rust/nf-sys/Cargo.toml` depends on all 12 engine crates (prism, cadence, splice, folio, pitch, tally, quill, photo, motion, design, draft, scene), so the step 1 archive contains every engine. A new studio that needs one engine still ships all 12 in the archive. UNVERIFIED: whether a feature flag trims that.

Engine contract tests need `@nyc-tron/ui` as a devDependency (URL tarball); apps do not.

### Step 3. `@nitro-forge/studio-layout`

Private, pure TypeScript, no build step (`"exports": {".": "./src/index.ts"}`). Used by `studio-workspace` (`model.ts`, `index.tsx`, `stage.tsx`, `app-manifest.ts`). Add `"@nitro-forge/studio-layout": "workspace:*"`. No tarball exists. Distribution is blocked on the versioning scheme in decision 3.

### Step 4. `@nitro-forge/icons`

`workspace:*` today. Peers (all optional in the package, required in practice): `react` >=19, `react-native` >=0.81, `react-native-svg` >=15. The root patches `react-native-svg@15.16.0` (`patches/react-native-svg@15.16.0.patch`); the example and `studio-workspace` pin 15.16.0. Entry points: `@nitro-forge/icons` (catalog and glyph data, headless), `@nitro-forge/icons/native` and `/web` (the `ForgeIcon` component).

### Step 5. NYC-Tron tarballs

Seven packages pinned in `tooling/nyc-tron.json`, release `v1.0.0-rc.2` of `mikevocalz/NYC-Tron-UI`, commit `0e09d3be8263b3dbb2eab1a78e5dd66b83b68e44`. They are GitHub release assets, not npm packages. The URL pattern is:

```
https://github.com/mikevocalz/NYC-Tron-UI/releases/download/v1.0.0-rc.2/nyc-tron-<name>-1.0.0-rc.2.tgz
```

| Package | Used by |
|---|---|
| `@nyc-tron/ui` | `studio-workspace` (dependency), `apps/example`, engine devDependencies |
| `@nyc-tron/core` | `apps/example` |
| `@nyc-tron/expo-controls` | `apps/example` (Select, NativePopover, NativeActionMenu) |
| `@nyc-tron/reserved-regions` | `apps/example` |
| `@nyc-tron/platform-services` | pinned, not in `apps/example` dependencies |
| `@nyc-tron/native-controls` | pinned, named in cadence comments, not in `apps/example` dependencies |
| `@nyc-tron/hardware-keys` | pinned, not in `apps/example` dependencies |

Put the exact URL in the consumer's `package.json` (`"@nyc-tron/ui": "<url>"`). The sha256 for each file is in `tooling/nyc-tron.json` and in the release's `SHA256SUMS`. Checks:

```bash
pnpm verify:nyc-tron                                  # node tooling/verify-nyc-tron-pin.mjs: manifests and lockfile use the pinned URL
node tooling/verify-nyc-tron-pin.mjs --download       # also re-hashes the release assets
```

The pin check requires dependency sections to use the exact URL and peer ranges to be caret ranges the pinned version satisfies.

Optional dev link to a local NYC-Tron checkout: `withNycTronDevLink(config, { projectRoot })` from `tooling/nyc-tron-metro.cjs`, active only when `NYC_TRON_ROOT` is set. Native modules still come from the installed tarball.

Peer set `studio-workspace` also needs: `zustand` 5.1.0, `react-native-gesture-handler` >=3.4 <4, and `react-native-reanimated` >=4.7.1 <5 (the turret's native motion file imports it; the package marks it optional). The example pins gesture-handler 3.5.0, reanimated 4.7.1 and `react-native-worklets` 0.13.1.

### Step 6. Theme CSS

`packages/studio-workspace/src/theme.css` and `theme.native.css` are generated and committed. Regenerate after editing `theme.ts`:

```bash
pnpm --filter @nitro-forge/studio-workspace build:theme   # node build-theme.mjs
```

Then import the right file:

- Expo with Uniwind (`apps/example/global.css`): `@import 'tailwindcss';`, `@import 'uniwind';`, then `@import '../../packages/studio-workspace/src/theme.native.css';`. Metro config wraps Expo's config with `withUniwindConfig(config, { cssEntryFile: './global.css', dtsFile: './src/uniwind-types.d.ts', polyfills: { rem: 14 } })`.
- Web with Vite and Tailwind 4 (`apps/studio-preview/src/style.css`): `@import "tailwindcss" important;`, `@source` lines for `packages/studio-workspace/src`, `node_modules/@nyc-tron/ui/dist/components` and `node_modules/@nyc-tron/expo-controls/dist/components` (NYC-Tron publishes only `dist/`, so Tailwind must scan it), then `@import` of `theme.css`.

NYC-Tron ships no colours. Its components read the semantic variables the generated CSS declares (`--color-primary`, `--color-surface-raised`, `--color-border`, `--color-text` and the rest). Without this step the controls render without brand colour. A registry add can copy the CSS files but cannot run the generator or edit the app's CSS entry file.

### Step 7. `StudioUIProvider` and host

Provider and host mapping, from `apps/example/src/studio-ui.tsx` and `apps/example/app/_layout.tsx`:

```tsx
import { Image, Pressable, ScrollView, Text, TextInput, View } from 'react-native';
import { ScopedVariables } from 'uniwind';
import { Select } from '@nyc-tron/expo-controls/Select';
import { NativePopover } from '@nyc-tron/expo-controls/NativePopover';
import { NativeActionMenu } from '@nyc-tron/expo-controls/NativeActionMenu';
import { nycTronStudioUI } from '@nitro-forge/studio-workspace/nyc-tron-host';

export const studioUI = nycTronStudioUI({
  View, Text, Pressable, Image, Select, ActionMenu: NativeActionMenu, NativePopover, GroupedSelect: Select,
  TokenScope: ({ variables, children }) => <ScopedVariables variables={variables}>{children}</ScopedVariables>,
  ScrollView: ScrollView as never, TextInput: TextInput as never,
});

// root layout
<StudioUIProvider components={studioUI}>{/* app */}</StudioUIProvider>
```

The example casts `ScrollView` and `TextInput` because React Native 0.88 types their refs as instance interfaces. The web host (`apps/studio-preview/src/studio-ui.tsx`) is the web counterpart and was not read for this document (UNVERIFIED).

### Step 8. Components

Only now do the registry items for studio chrome work: `forge-workspace`, `prism-editor`, `persona-turret` and the rest.

## Registry add versus tarball or native install

| Needs | Registry add | Tarball, workspace or native install |
|---|---|---|
| Copy `forge-workspace`, `prism-editor`, `persona-*`, `forge-directions`, `studio-theme` sources | Yes | |
| Copy `forge-icon`, `forge-icon-button`, `studio-ui-provider`, `nyc-tron-host` sources | Yes | |
| Install `react-native-svg`, `zustand`, gesture-handler, reanimated | Yes, as npm dependencies of the item | |
| Run `build-theme.mjs` | | Yes (a script, and it imports `theme.ts` directly) |
| Edit the app's CSS entry and Metro config | | Yes (app code) |
| `@nyc-tron/*` packages | Items declare `registryDependencies`; the packages themselves are GitHub tarball URLs | Yes |
| `@nitro-forge/ignition`: Nitrogen codegen, `ForgeRust.xcframework`, Android static archives, CMake, podspec, Swift package | | Yes (decision 4) |
| Engine packages and their Rust crates | | Yes (decision 3) |
| `@nitro-forge/studio-layout` | | Yes (decision 3) |
| Quill, Tally, Splice and Prism binding adapters | Deferred | Need the engine facade first |
| Expo config plugin for brand identity (`tooling/brand/plugin.cjs`) | | Yes, not in registry scope |

Two items need a native prerequisite even though their own files are plain TypeScript. `prism-editor` imports `base64ToBytes` and `bytesToBase64` from the `@nitro-forge/ignition` package index, so a copy of it resolves only after step 1. `forge-workspace`, `forge-document-stage` and `studio-layout` consumers need `@nitro-forge/studio-layout` from step 3 for the `Studio` type and the dock model.

## Known gaps in the chain

- No document today gives these steps in order. This file is the first.
- Steps 1 to 3 cannot be reproduced outside the monorepo: no tarball or release exists for `ignition`, the engines or `studio-layout`.
- The Apple archive script and the integration doc disagree on Intel simulator support (step 1).
- Seven NYC-Tron packages are pinned; the example installs four. Which of the other three a new studio needs is not stated in the repo. UNVERIFIED.


<!-- file: SKILL.md -->
---
name: nitro-forge
description: Install and use the Nitro Forge studio components (workspace chrome, persona turret, Prism editor, theme, StudioUIProvider, icons) through the @nitro-forge shadcn registry. Use when adding a Forge item, wiring StudioUIProvider, rebranding the accent, checking a token, or deciding why an engine or ignition cannot be installed with shadcn.
---

# Nitro Forge

Nitro Forge is a set of document studios on one Rust engine. The `@nitro-forge` registry ships the studio UI as source files. The engines, `@nitro-forge/ignition` and `@nitro-forge/studio-layout` are not in it. Controls such as Button and TabBar come from the `@nyc-tron` registry, which owns them.

## Provider prerequisite: do this first

Every studio component throws "No substitute UI is installed" at first render unless the app is wrapped once in `StudioUIProvider`. Install the provider and a host before any component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4.23.0 add @nitro-forge/studio-ui-provider @nitro-forge/nyc-tron-host
```

Then fill the 27 slots with `nycTronStudioUI()` from the installed `nyc-tron-host` file and wrap the root layout:

```tsx
<StudioUIProvider components={studioUI}>{/* app */}</StudioUIProvider>
```

The host needs the `@nyc-tron` controls and three host parts (`Select`, `NativePopover`, `NativeActionMenu` from `@nyc-tron/expo-controls`). The wiring is app code, so shadcn cannot do it. The working example is `apps/example/src/studio-ui.tsx` in the repo.

Items that need the provider are marked `meta.needsProvider: true` in `r/<item>.json`. Items that do not: `studio-gesture`, `persona-model`, `instrument-system`, `workspace-utilities`, `studio-theme`, `forge-directions`, `forge-icon`, `forge-icon-button`, `brand-theme`.

## Install order

Nine steps, numbered 0 to 8. A registry add covers step 4 and step 8, plus the file part of steps 5, 6 and 7.

| Step | What | `shadcn add` |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Toolchain: Node >=24.3.0, pnpm 12.18.0, Rust, Xcode or Android NDK with `cargo-ndk` | no |
| 1 | `@nitro-forge/ignition` native host | no (decision 4) |
| 2 | An engine package, for example `@nitro-forge/tally` | no (decision 3) |
| 3 | `@nitro-forge/studio-layout` | no (decision 3) |
| 4 | `@nitro-forge/icons` as item `forge-icon` | yes |
| 5 | NYC-Tron tarballs from `tooling/nyc-tron.json` | packages no, wrapper items yes |
| 6 | Theme CSS from `studio-theme` | files yes, the generator and CSS import no |
| 7 | `StudioUIProvider` and host | files yes, wiring no |
| 8 | Studio components | yes |

Steps 1 to 3 cannot be reproduced outside this monorepo today. No tag, release or tarball exists for them, nothing is on npm, and `compatibility.v1.json` records distribution as not run. Stop and ask rather than invent a release URL. The commands for steps 0 to 3, 5 and 6 are in `docs/agent-native/install-order.md`. They were read from the repo and were not run on the machine that wrote this skill.

Items that name a prerequisite shadcn cannot install list it in `meta.prerequisites` and in the `docs` text the CLI prints after an add. `prism-editor` needs `@nitro-forge/ignition` (it imports `base64ToBytes` and `bytesToBase64`). `forge-workspace`, `forge-document-stage` and `workspace-utilities` need `@nitro-forge/studio-layout`, and so does everything that depends on them.

## Commands

Verified against a local server with shadcn CLI 4.23.0, in an app whose `components.json` maps both namespaces:

```bash
npx shadcn@4.23.0 list @nitro-forge
npx shadcn@4.23.0 view @nitro-forge/persona-composer
npx shadcn@4.23.0 add @nitro-forge/persona-composer
npx shadcn@4.23.0 mcp
```

`components.json` at the repo root points the two namespaces at `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mikevocalz/<repo>/<ref>/r/{name}.json`. `<ref>` is `nitroForgeRef` (`master`) for `@nitro-forge` and `nycTronRef` (`main`) for `@nyc-tron`, both in `tooling/registry/config.json`. They are moving branches, not release tags, until the owner cuts tags: what an install fetches changes with each push, and the `@nyc-tron` items resolve only once NYC-Tron's `r/` is on its `main` branch. To pin, run `node tooling/registry/set-ref.mjs <nitroForgeRef> [nycTronRef]`; it rewrites the config and regenerates every generated file. The install proof against a local server accepted `text/plain` responses, which is what raw.githubusercontent.com serves. A live fetch from raw GitHub has not been done. `.mcp.json` runs `npx shadcn@latest mcp` because the mission specifies it. Pin it to `shadcn@4.23.0`, the version the registry is built with, if you want a reproducible tool version.

Item names keep slashes: `@nyc-tron/forge/layers/LayerStack`. The `@nyc-tron` item names are the export keys after `./components/`. All 22 that Forge depends on exist in NYC-Tron's built `registry.json`; `check-imports` reads that registry on every run.

Installed files land in `components/forge/` (icons in `components/forge/icons/`). Imports between them are relative. Imports of NYC-Tron files are written as `@/components/nyc-tron/ui/components/<key>`, which is where the `@nyc-tron` items install (their `files[].target` is `@components/nyc-tron/ui/components/<key>.tsx`, and `@components` expands to your `components` alias).

## Rebrand contract

A brand sets three keys per scheme in `brand.theme.json`: `accent`, `ink` and `soft`. Together they feed `--color-primary`, `--color-accent`, `--color-focus`, `--color-on-primary` and `--color-primary-tint`. That is 6 values.

```json
{
  "dark": { "accent": "#66B9FF", "ink": "#081D2F", "soft": "#173C59" },
  "light": { "accent": "#086CB8", "ink": "#FFFFFF", "soft": "#D6EAFB" },
  "defaultDensity": "standard"
}
```

Install `brand-theme` for the schema and the checker. `brandThemeProblems(file)` returns the locked keys it finds, colours that are not six hex digits and a `defaultDensity` outside `compact`, `standard`, `comfortable`. `checkBrandTheme(file)` always returns six entries and never throws: it measures `ink` on `accent` (4.5:1), `accent` as a focus ring on the raised surface (3:1) and `text` on `soft` (4.5:1), and an incomplete file gives entries with `pass: false`, `ratio: null` and a `problem`.

A brand reaches the UI through two channels. Apply both.

| Channel | Call | Reaches | Does not reach |
|---|---|---|---|
| CSS variables | `brandCssVariables(theme, scheme)` on a `[data-brand]` block, `:root` or a `TokenScope` | NYC-Tron controls (Button, TabBar, SegmentedControl, Select, Banner) and Tailwind utilities reading `--color-primary`, `--color-accent`, `--color-focus`, `--color-on-primary`, `--color-primary-tint` | Colours Forge reads in JavaScript |
| JS overrides | `brandThemeOverrides(theme, scheme)` as `themeOverrides` on `ForgeWorkspace` | Workspace header, rail label, studio glyphs and the soft chip behind them | The CSS variables |

`PersonaTurret` (reads `colors.accent`) and `PersonaComposer` (reads `colors.accent` and `colors.soft`) take their own `colors` prop, which `ForgeWorkspace` does not fill, so pass the same overrides there. `PrismEditor`, `QuillTextEditor`, `ForgeDocumentStage` and the default `ForgeIcon` palette are reached by neither channel today. Installing `brand-theme` and applying only the CSS variables recolours the controls and leaves the workspace header, glyphs and turret on the old accent. The file is separate from `tooling/brand/brand.schema.json`, which stays closed and feeds the Expo plugin (decision 24).

Deferred: the six neutral keys (`base`, `raised`, `deep`, `line`, `text`, `muted`) wait for an owner-supplied contrast check (decision 23). Struck: any radius override, because chrome keeps 4 px. Locked: status colours, `paper*`, every scale and hit target.

## Token rules

- Use the CSS variables from `studio-theme`, for example `--color-surface-raised`, not a hex value. `docs/agent-native/tokens.map.json` lists 234 proposed tokens with their dark and light values.
- Every token carries the exact value of the literal it replaces, so tokenizing changes no pixel. Spacing keys are unit multiples (`space.2`, `space.1.5`), the same numbering as Tailwind.
- Colour drift stays as separate tokens: icon accent `#6859E8` against workspace accent `#6950D1`, Prism blue against the launcher purple, stage paper `#F7F5ED` against `#FFFEFC`. Unifying them changes pixels and is the owner's call (decisions 5, 20, 26, 27).
- Do not add a hex literal, a numeric style literal, a numeric JSX size prop, a Tailwind arbitrary value or a `fs(x + n)` offset to a file under `packages/`. `tooling/codemod/check-no-hardcoded.mjs` enforces exactly that list (its header is the definition). It is not a claim that no number remains: SVG geometry, data arrays, native Kotlin and Swift, `apps/` and tests are out of its scope, and 76 findings in 53 lines are allowlisted in `tooling/codemod/allowlist.json`, each with the reason no existing same-valued token fits.
- Registry files are generated. Import specifiers are rewritten only in `r/*.json` (decision 39). The repo source keeps `@nyc-tron/ui/components/...` imports.

## Accessibility status

Values are `reviewed-pass`, `reviewed-fail` and `unverified`. Nothing was rendered, so no item is `verified`. Of the 17 admitted items, 6 are reviewed-pass, 10 are reviewed-fail and 1 (`nyc-tron-host`) is unverified. The failures are listed per item in `meta.a11yFailures` and in each page's A11y section. Examples: light muted text on base at 4.43:1 in `forge-workspace`; a ghost label at 1.11:1 in `prism-canvas`; status changes only colour in `forge-icon`.

## Icons

`forge-icon` ships 47 drawn glyphs. 42 of the 1,463 catalog ids resolve to one, and 6 drawn glyphs are not catalog ids. A name with no glyph renders nothing. Never describe the catalog as 1,463 available icons.

## Not in the registry, and why

- Four binding adapters (`quill-office-binding`, `tally-sheet-binding`, `splice-timeline-binding`, `prism-canvas-binding`): each imports its engine facade, which a registry add cannot install (decision 30).
- Twelve engines (prism, cadence, splice, folio, pitch, tally, quill, photo, motion, design, draft, scene): they need the Rust binary through ignition and ship as release tarballs at 0.0.0 (decision 3).
- `ignition`: shadcn cannot run nitrogen, pod install or CMake (decision 4).
- `studio-layout`: private workspace package with no tarball.

`registry-excluded.json` holds each reason and the condition for returning. Engine and foundation pages are in `docs/engines/`.

## Rebuild after a source change

```bash
node tooling/registry/build.mjs
node tooling/registry/check-imports.mjs
node tooling/registry/validate-registry.mjs
node tooling/docs/build-docs.mjs
node tooling/docs/check-docs.mjs
```

`build.mjs` runs `shadcn build` through `npx` unless `SHADCN_BIN` points at a local shadcn 4.23.0 binary. Never edit `r/`, `registry.json`, `docs/components/` or `llms.txt` by hand. CI fails when a rebuild changes them.

## Where to read more

- `llms.txt` for the page index and `llms-full.txt` for all pages in one file.
- `docs/components/<item>.md` for props, states, accessibility and examples.
- `docs/agent-native/install-order.md` and `docs/agent-native/02-design-system.md`.
